title: The Flour

where.detail: at his cot in the infirmary hall, the kitchen novice still kneeling over the flour at the undercroft door

time: the dawn bell and the hour after it, the morning after the eve
last_beat: "Make your mind up, Captain," he said. "He's not getting any warmer."

people.did: Read the flour at the undercroft door before the House could step in it; held the House back from taking the door off its pins without the Prior, and sent the eager ones to carry wood up the bell tower; waited for Maelis to speak of the stair, and she did not.
people.now: At his cot in the hall. The House knows the cold comes up every night through the gap under the undercroft door, and it is waiting on him to say how the stair is taken.

facts.fact: He read the flour by a lamp held low on the flags: no print in it or out, but a half-moon of frost glazed into it from the gap, every grain leaning toward the door.
facts.evidence: every grain of that glaze caught the light the same way, all of them leaning, as if the floor had been combed toward the door in the night

facts.fact: He believes something on the other side draws on the hall through the gap; the novice said breathed on, he said breathed in.
He would not let the House take the undercroft door off its pins without the Prior, who has the key.
facts.evidence: Nobody touches this door without the Prior. She has the key.

facts.fact: He sent the lay brother from the fire and the young ones with the mallet to carry wood up the bell tower for Sister Pell instead.
facts.evidence: If you want something to carry, carry that.

facts.fact: Told he would want to be first down the stair, he said he would be first down and the last to arrive.
facts.evidence: I'll just be the last to arrive.

people.did: Rang the hours through the night and came down between every bell to sit by the undercroft door; heard nothing come or go; told Hollis she would sleep after the noon bell.
people.now: Gone up to her bell tower after the dawn bell, her palms raw from the rope; the lay brothers are carrying wood up to her.

facts.fact: She climbed the bell tower and came back down to sit by the undercroft door eight times between the night bell and the dawn bell.
facts.evidence: Up the tower. Ring. Down the stair. Sit. Up again. Eight times.

facts.fact: Nothing came through the undercroft door or went in that night, by her ear.
facts.evidence: Nothing came through that door, Captain, and nothing went in.

facts.fact: Her palms are rubbed red by the rope in two straight lines.
facts.evidence: they were red across the palms in two straight lines

people.did: Read the knee at the hour and asked what it did this morning; said nothing of the stair, though she saw him waiting for it; told him to ask if he wanted to ask, and went to the far cots without a lamp.
people.now: At the far cots. She has not spoken of the stair, and has told the Captain to ask her outright if he wants something.

facts.fact: She let the Captain wait for her to speak of the stair, and did not.
She told him that if he wants to ask her something he should ask it, and that she would be at the far cots.
facts.evidence: If you want to ask me something, ask it. I'll be at the far cots.

people.did: Counted the flour: no prints in or out, frost; said the seam on the wall sweats every dawn she has looked; sat by the Captain afterwards, not counting.
people.now: Sitting on the end of the cot next to the Captain's with her ledger shut, waiting on him.

facts.fact: She counted no prints into the flour and none out, and frost.
facts.evidence: "Prints in," she said. "None. Prints out. None. Frost."

facts.fact: She says the seam on the wall sweats every dawn since she started looking, so this is not new: only the first night anyone sat up with it.
facts.evidence: It's not new. It's just the first night anyone sat up with it.

people.did: At the Grey Cot with the lad's hand; told Sister Pell to go and get some sleep, heard himself, and closed his hand on the lad's; told the Captain to make his mind up.
people.now: At the Grey Cot with the lad's hand, waiting on the Captain's decision about the stair.

facts.fact: He told Sister Pell to go and get some sleep, heard himself say it, and his hand closed slowly on the lad's.
He told the Captain to make his mind up, because the lad is not getting any warmer.

fired.evidence: "Go and get some sleep, sister," he said. "The door'll keep."

now.against: Something below the hall draws on it every night through the gap under the undercroft door, and the only man the House waits on cannot go down a stair.
